@Sebastian Ullrich and I are excited to share the news of the Lean Focused Research Organization (FRO)! A new nonprofit dedicated to advancing the Formal Mathematics revolution, we aim to tackle the challenges of scalability, usability, and proof automation in the Lean proof assistant. Our 5-year mission is to empower Lean towards self-sustainability.

We gratefully acknowledge philanthropic support from the Simons Foundation International, the Alfred P. Sloan Foundation, and Richard Merkin.

To discover more about Focused Research Organizations, please visit convergentresearch.org.
Too bad it’s an LLC and not a German GmbH, else we could call it the Lean FRO G :frog:

:tada: The Lean FRO welcomes @Mac Malone and @Scott Morrison to its team. As you may know, both Mac and Scott have already made invaluable contributions to the Lean ecosystem and we are excited that they will now be able to drive it forward full-time!
Congratulations!
Lovely, welcome @Mac Malone and @Scott Morrison

The Lean FRO is happy to announce that it has taken over maintenance of the Lean and mathlib benchmarking infrastructure, now located at speed.lean-fro.org, and is providing a new high-end benchmarking machine for it. We thank the Programming Paradigms group at the Karlsruhe Institute of Technology for their preceding sponsorship.
Sebastian didn't say just how big an improvement his new machine is: "total run down from 2:23h to 0:31h"!!
at that rate it might actually be able to catch up with the humans generating and merging PRs faster than the benchmark bot can time
There have been at most 30 Mathlib PRs being merged per day, so the hope is that this machine can keep up with commits to master on mathilb4 and lean4, as well as explicit !bench commands. We'll see!
Is this in the cloud :tm: or actually physically hosted somewhere?

Convergent Research is a member of the Schmidt Futures Network and Eric Schmidt seems to be aiming at something bigger:

Eric Schmidt is reportedly building a giant nonprofit startup for AI+Science. Quote: "the effort is modeled after OpenAI [...] which was founded with great fanfare as a philanthropic organization."

https://twitter.com/DrJimFan/status/1692599906526019951
:tada: @Marc Huisinga has joined the Lean FRO today! Marc is one of the creators of the Lean language server as well as the author of Static Uniqueness Analysis for the Lean 4 Theorem Prover
Is there a specific area where Marc intends to work?

Patrick Massot said:

Is there a specific area where Marc intends to work?

For now, I intend to work on the VSCode extension and the language server :)
Great! What do you want to improve there?
Will we get import autocompletion and quick fix?

I want to work towards ensuring that using Lean both as a theorem prover and as a programming language is at the very least on par with the user interface of other programming languages and theorem provers. That also includes topics like import autocompletion or quickfixes, but also e.g. the initial setup of Lean.
I think import completion is a rather important target. It is literally the very first thing you encounter when starting a Lean file. And, in Lean 4, an error there blocks everything.
Update on save would be a nice feature to have too.

One important part of the “user interface” is error messages, which IMO are quite confusing right now, but that might be a different person’s job to work on. Although Im curious how the rust langauge server handles their error messages which simaltqneuously reference multiple parts of the file.
I have a silly question: is Lean FRO an intentional pun on Swedish linfrö?
No

The Lean FRO welcomes its newest employee, @David Thrane Christiansen! David is the author of Functional Programming in Lean and co-author of The Little Typer. He had second-most commits on the first version of Idris, he's worked in industry on software verification tools at Galois, and as the Haskell Foundation's Executive Director.
Wonderful! Does it mean we'll get even more great documentation?
Both documentation and tools to make producing it easier are part of my tasks, so if I'm successful, then you'll get more. I'll let you be the judge of its greatness :-)

I'm happy to announce https://live.lean-lang.org/, the official online playground for Lean 4 + std/mathlib hosted by the Lean FRO and based on lean4web by @Alexander Bentkamp and @Jon Eugster. Many thanks to Alex for helping with the setup!
I've just realised that I can now run lean code on my phone again, as a consequence of this. I just used exact? to solve a problem on stack exchange after import Mathlib and it worked immediately!

The Lean FRO welcomes @Joe Hendrix to its team! Joe developed binary verification tools in Lean 4 at Galois. This was one of the first external uses of Lean 4. Joe most recently was a Principal Computer Scientist at SRI and contributed to SRI's automated verification tools.

@Joachim Breitner has joined the Lean FRO today! Joachim has already posted why he is excited for this new position on his blog: https://www.joachim-breitner.de/blog/809-Joining_the_Lean_FRO. We are just as excited!

@Kyle Miller has joined our team on a part-time position concurrent to his post-doc at the University of California! He is already working on high-priority issues for the community such as the soon-to-be-released lean4#2778.

Starting next Wednesday (Feb 14), we would like to provide a new way for Lean users to get help with technical questions: join our weekly "office hour" video meeting to ask team members of the Lean FRO directly! We will start with Leo and me next week and then mix up hosts and time zones in further weeks. See https://lean-fro.org/events/ for more details.
What sort of topics are expected to be in scope for these office hours?
I think we'll find out what works best as we go but as long as it's a not-too-broad question about a topic that you can reasonably expect one of the hosts to know about, that should be good

The Lean FRO is happy to welcome Sofia Rodrigues and Henrik Böving as our newest part-time team members! Sofia has previously developed an entire ecosystem of Lean packages for a backend challenge. Henrik is the creator of doc-gen4 among other valuable contributions to Lean's ecosystem.

(also, next office hour tomorrow!)
We're thrilled to welcome Corinna Calhoun as our new COO! With an extensive background in leadership at both Microsoft and Amazon, Corinna brings unparalleled experience and vision to our mission.
@Markus Himmel is our newest team member starting this week! Markus is a Mathlib maintainer and has worked on industrial applications of formal methods.
In addition, the Lean FRO is looking for a Principal engineer! https://lean-fro.org/jobs/

Not personally interested, but is the Principal Engineer position aimed at any specific points in the FRO Roadmap or is it generic? What are the main duties? Also, the link https://jobs.lever.co/convergentresearch/2e3abd63-4893-4b15-8bad-187920c86e12 fails to load for me.

We are thrilled to announce that @Johan Commelin has joined the Lean FRO this week! Johan likely will not need any introduction for most people around here, but for the sake of completeness, he is a Mathlib maintainer and is well-known for leading the Liquid Tensor Experiment. He will be a key contributor to the ongoing growth and improvements of Mathlib.
I don't think these have officially made it to here yet, so: we've recently written about our Year 1 in Review as well as published our updated Year 2 Roadmap

We are excited to welcome Bharat Bhat to the Lean FRO. His background at Microsoft, Okta, and InfluxData is uniquely suited to help Lean reach more developers. Stay tuned for more news and announcements from Bharat in the coming weeks and months.

We are excited to announce that @Cameron Zwarich and @Ashley Blacquiere (yes, that's me :grinning:) have joined the Lean FRO this month!

Cameron has over 15 years of experience at Apple working on low-level systems software and is the creator of Rosetta 2. He will be focusing on improving Lean's code generator. Ashley has over 15 years experience working in post-secondary education and the video game industry and is joining the team as Operations Manager.

:note: Fun fact: Although Cameron currently resides in the US, both Cameron and Ashley are Canadian and are the first Canadian employees of the Lean FRO, which now includes employees in :flag_australia: Australia, :flag_brazil: Brazil, :flag_canada: Canada, :flag_denmark: Denmark, :flag_germany: Germany, :flag_netherlands: the Netherlands and :flag_united_states: the US!

The Lean FRO welcomes :three: new research software engineers to the team this week!:

  1. @Joseph Rotella has been a Lean user since 2021 and has worked on projects related to functional programming, math education, and AI.
  2. @Paul Reichert has partially formalized his thesis in Lean and has worked on a constraint solver.
  3. @Sebastian Graf just finished his PhD on static program analysis and has been a developer of the Glasgow Haskell Compiler for 7 years.

We're excited to Joseph, Paul and Sebastian into the FRO and look forward to their continued !

:megaphone: We welcomed another new team member to the Lean FRO last week: Wojciech Ròżowski is currently finishing his PhD at University College London supervised by Alexandra Silva and Samson Abramsky and his interests are centred around formal verification and semantics of programming languages.

:earth_africa: Wojciech is the first :flag_united_kingdom: -based employee of Lean FRO (and happy to say hi to any Lean crowd in #Geographic locality > London, England )

I'm happy to share that the Department of Computer Science at the University of Oxford has recently released recordings of the Strachey Series Lectures delivered in a double-bill by @Leonardo de Moura and @Kevin Buzzard on May 6. You can see the lecture recordings here:

  • Leo: Formalizing the Future: Lean’s Impact on Mathematics, Programming, and AI
  • Kevin: Will Computers prove theorems?

For interest sake, here are all recordings of the Strachey Lecture Series going back to 2015.
A message was moved from this topic to #general > Lean in the wild by Eric Wieser.

For the last several months team members at the Lean FRO have been working on the development of a new lean-lang.org website. I'm pleased to say that we've "soft launched" the new website today!

The website has gone through several iterations internally with the Lean FRO team, and with some community members, but this "soft launch" is our first test of the site in a truly live fashion. Our plan is to observe the site over the next day or so before making a more public official launch statement on Monday.

To that end, we welcome feedback, especially any feedback identifying breaking or nonstandard behaviour. I've created a discussion thread for that purpose: #general > Discussion: New lean-lang.org

Our goal with this new site is to modernize the design and to update all critical informational pages, but we don't necessarily think of it as a static offering. Over the coming months we'll continue to implement usability and content improvements. Feel free to provide feedback along those lines as well, though our immediate concern will be in ensuring that the website is stable before the official Monday launch.

We hope you like the new lean-lang.org!

We’re excited to share some big news:

Alex Gerko, CEO of XTX Markets, is donating $10M to the Lean FRO and the new Mathlib Initiative, backing our shared mission to make machine-checked mathematics and formal verification practical and accessible.

At the Lean FRO, we will develop a next-generation mathematical workbench for the Lean theorem prover, an environment where mathematicians can collaborate using familiar informal writing, with the rigor and correctness guarantees of Lean. More info to come as we release our new Year 3 roadmap in a few weeks.

We're grateful to Alex Gerko, Convergent Research and all our other funders for their support, and we're thrilled to see Mathlib recognized for its incredible, community-driven contributions :heart:.

The full press release is available on the Renaissance Philanthropy website.

We're pleased to welcome @Jason Reed to the Lean FRO today!

Jason brings valuable experience in proof assistant implementation, tooling and web infrastructure development. In his previous work, Jason contributed to GitHub's CodeQL VS Code plugin and created an open source web sandbox for Twelf - a logical framework developed by Frank Pfenning and collaborators at Carnegie Mellon.

And we're excited to say that Jason will be leading the development of the next-generation mathematical workbench project, made possible through the funding from Alex Gerko, CEO of XTX Markets, announced last week.

Yesterday was @Joseph Rotella's last day with Lean FRO as he begins work on a PhD this fall at Northeastern University. This was always the plan, so not a surprise, but it's nevertheless :sad: to see Joseph go.

I wanted to take a moment to acknowledge the work Joseph did while at Lean FRO: Joseph was tasked with improving Lean error messages and his contributions have served to systematize our collection and development of error messages, as we all as improve their content and structure. This has unquestionably produced a positive meaningful impact on the Lean user experience, and will no doubt continue to do so into the future!

Thanks, Joseph, for all your contributions! We wish you the best of luck in your PhD studies and beyond!

We're excited to share the Lean FRO Year 3 roadmap today! This roadmap builds on work completed in the first two years of Lean FRO operations and will guide all development on Lean through July 2026.
Discussion at #general > Discussion: Lean FRO roadmap, year 3

The Lean FRO welcomed a new research software engineer to the team this week! @Joscha Mennicken recently completed his Masters thesis on KeYmaera X, previously his Bachelors thesis on the Lean LSP, and is one of the original devs of the Lean and Mathlib speedcenters (i.e. VelCom).

A big welcome to Joscha! We're looking forward to all his future contributions!

A big welcome to @Rob Simmons who joins the Lean FRO team this week! :tada:

Rob is a computer scientist with expertise in compilers, logic programming languages, and education. He has contributed to the design and implementation of the C0 programming languages used in introductory computer science courses at Carnegie Mellon and elsewhere, designed and implemented the Camperdown markup language used by Brilliant.org to build its math, science, and computer science educational content, and implemented the Dusa logic programming language that was presented at the POPL 2025 conference. He has experience as a product manager, project engineer, and software engineer in industry and academic settings, most recently teaching the software engineering course as a part-time lecturer at Northeastern University.

Rob will be working directly with @Jason Reed on the next-generation mathematical workbench project announced last month. Congrats and welcome, Rob!

Anyone regularly reading the #announce channel knows that @Johan Commelin has been named one of the directors of the Mathlib Initiative, and that @Anne Baanen has recently joined MI as well. On the Lean FRO side, this has become official over the last two weeks, so now seems like the right time to recognize their departure and acknowledge their contributions.

On behalf of the Lean FRO, I want to thank both Johan and Anne for their tremendous work and dedication to Lean, which extends to many years before the inauguration of the Lean FRO. While we will no longer have the pleasure of working directly with Johan and Anne on a daily basis, we very much look forward to future close collaboration and continuing our collective efforts - and with the entire MI team! - in their new capacity.

I'm happy to say that Lean FRO recently welcomed @Emilio Jesús Gallego Arias as our newest senior research software engineer working on the recently announced next-generation mathematical workbench project. :tada:

Emilio is a computer scientist with a background in programming languages and formal verification. He is a long-time fan of functional programming, interactive theorem proving, and open source communities, and is passionate about user and developer experience. For over 10 years, he has been a core contributor to the Rocq Prover, where he has built tools including jsRocq, Rocq-SerAPI, rocq-lsp, Dune's Rocq build language, and pétanque.

Please join me in welcoming Emilio!

I'm happy to announce that @𝚠𝚘𝚓𝚌𝚒𝚎𝚌𝚑 𝚗𝚊𝚠𝚛𝚘𝚌𝚔𝚒 has joined the Lean FRO this week as our newest senior research software engineer. Wojciech will be working on the next-generation mathematical workbench project. :tada:

Wojciech first got excited about Lean in 2019, and has been contributing to the system ever since. He co-designed early versions of the language server and VSCode editor extension for Lean 4, as well as the widgets framework and ProofWidgets library which he continues to actively maintain. He recently earned his PhD in logic from Carnegie Mellon University, with a dissertation focused on the certification of results in computer-aided mathematics.

Please join me in welcoming Wojciech!
